entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8294"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 8</title> <div sID="gen13153" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="Song.8.1-Song.8.14">So 8:1-14</reference>.<div eID="gen13153" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13154" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8294"/>1. He had been a brother already. Why, then, this prayer here? It refers to the time after His resurrection, when the previous outward intimacy with Him was no longer allowed, but it was implied it should be renewed at the second coming (<reference osisRef="John.20.17">Joh 20:17</reference>). For this the Church here prays; meanwhile she enjoys inward spiritual communion with Him. The last who ever "kissed" Jesus Christ on earth was the traitor Judas. The bride's return with the King to her mother's house answers to <reference osisRef="Acts.8.25">Ac 8:25</reference>, after the mission to Samaria. The rest spoken of (<reference osisRef="Song.8.4">So 8:4</reference>) answers to <reference osisRef="Acts.9.31">Ac 9:31</reference>.<div eID="gen13154" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13155" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">that sucked ... mother--</hi>a brother born of the same mother; the closest tie. <div eID="gen13155" type="x-p"/>

Her desire to bring Him into her home circle (<reference osisRef="John.1.41">Joh 1:41</reference>).<div eID="gen13156" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13157" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">who would instruct me--</hi>rather, "thou wouldest instruct me," namely, how I might best please thee (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.2">Is 11:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.11.3">3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.50.4">50:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.12.12">Lu 12:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.14.26">Joh 14:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.16.13">16:13</reference>).<div eID="gen13157" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13158" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">spiced wine--</hi>seasoned with aromatic perfumes. Jesus Christ ought to have our choicest gifts. Spices are never introduced in the song in His absence; therefore the time of His return from "the mountain of spices" (<reference osisRef="Song.8.14">So 8:14</reference>) is contemplated. Till then the believer often cannot feel towards, or speak of, Him as he would wish. <div eID="gen13158" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8296"/><div sID="gen13159" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8296"/>3-4. The "left and right hand," &c., occurred only once actually (<reference osisRef="Song.2.6">So 2:6</reference>), and here optatively. Only at His first manifestation did the Church palpably embrace Him; at His second coming there shall be again sensible communion with Him. The rest in <reference osisRef="Song.8.4">So 8:4</reference>, which is a spiritual realization of the wish in <reference osisRef="Song.8.3">So 8:3</reference> (<reference osisRef="1Pet.1.8">1Pe 1:8</reference>), and the charge not to disturb it, close the first, second, and fourth canticles; not the third, as the bridegroom there takes charge Himself; nor the fifth, as, if repose formed its close, we might mistake the present state for our rest. The broken, longing close, like that of the whole Bible (<reference osisRef="Rev.22.20">Re 22:20</reference>), reminds us we are to be waiting for a Saviour to come. On "daughters of Jerusalem," see on <reference osisRef="Song.7.10">So 7:10</reference>.<div eID="gen13159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13160" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Canticle V.--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Song.8.5-Song.8.14">So 8:5-14</reference>)--From The Call of the Gentiles to the Close of Revelation. <div eID="gen13160" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8297"/><div sID="gen13161" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8297"/><hi type="bold">5. Who is this--</hi>Words of the daughters of Jerusalem, that is, the churches of Judea; referring to Paul, on his return from Arabia ("the wilderness"), whither he had gone after conversion (<reference osisRef="Gal.1.15-Gal.1.24">Ga 1:15-24</reference>).<div eID="gen13161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13162" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I raised thee ... she ... bare thee--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Acts.26.14-Acts.26.16">Ac 26:14-16</reference>). The first words of Jesus Christ to the bride since her going to the garden of nuts (<reference osisRef="Song.6.9">So 6:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Song.6.10">10</reference>); so His appearance to Paul is the only one since His ascension, <reference osisRef="Song.8.13">So 8:13</reference> is not an address of Him as visible: her reply implies He is not visible (<reference osisRef="1Cor.15.8">1Co 15:8</reference>). Spiritually, she was found in the moral wilderness (<reference osisRef="Ezek.16.5">Eze 16:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.13.5">Ho 13:5</reference>); but now she is "coming up from" it (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.2">Jr 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.14">Ho 2:14</reference>), especially in the last stage of her journey, her conscious weakness casting itself the more wholly on Jesus Christ (<reference osisRef="2Cor.12.9">2Co 12:9</reference>). "Raised" (<reference osisRef="Eph.2.1-Eph.2.7">Ep 2:1-7</reference>). Found ruined under the forbidden tree (<reference osisRef="Gen.3.22-Gen.3.24">Ge 3:22-24</reference>); restored under the shadow of Jesus Christ crucified, "the green tree" (<reference osisRef="Luke.23.31">Lu 23:31</reference>), fruit-"bearing" by the cross (<reference osisRef="Isa.53.11">Is 53:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.12.24">Joh 12:24</reference>). "Born again by the Holy Ghost" "there" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.16.3-Ezek.16.6">Eze 16:3-6</reference>). In this verse, her dependence, in the similar verse, <reference osisRef="Song.3.6">So 3:6</reference>, &c., His omnipotence to support her, are brought out (<reference osisRef="Deut.33.26">De 33:26</reference>). <div eID="gen13162" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 5. Who is this-- Words of the daughters of Jerusalem, that is, the churches of Judea; referring to Paul, on his return from Arabia ("the wilderness"), whither he had gone after conversion ( Ga 1:15-24 ). I raised thee ... she ... bare thee-- ( Ac 26:14-16 ). The first words of Jesus Christ to the bride since her going to the garden of nuts ( So 6:9 , 10 ); so His appearance to Paul is the only one since His ascension, So 8:13 is not an address of Him as visible: her reply implies He is not visible ( 1Co 15:8 ). Spiritually, she was found in the moral wilderness ( Eze 16:5 ; Ho 13:5 ); but now she is "coming up from" it ( Jr 2:2 ; Ho 2:14 ), especially in the last stage of her journey, her conscious weakness casting itself the more wholly on Jesus Christ ( 2Co 12:9 ). "Raised" ( Ep 2:1-7 ). Found ruined under the forbidden tree ( Ge 3:22-24 ); restored under the shadow of Jesus Christ crucified, "the green tree" ( Lu 23:31 ), fruit-"bearing" by the cross ( Is 53:11 ; Joh 12:24 ). "Born again by the Holy Ghost" "there" ( Eze 16:3-6 ). In this verse, her dependence, in the similar verse, So 3:6 , &c., His omnipotence to support her, are brought out ( De 33:26 ).

Implying approaching absence of the Bridegroom.<div eID="gen13163" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13164" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">seal--</hi>having her name and likeness engraven on it. His Holy Priesthood also in heaven (<reference osisRef="Exod.28.6-Exod.12.15">Ex 28:6-12, 15</reference>-<reference osisRef="Exod.12.30">30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.4.14">He 4:14</reference>); "his heart" there answering to "thine heart" here, and "two shoulders" to "arm." (Compare <reference osisRef="Jer.22.24">Jr 22:24</reference>, with <reference osisRef="Hag.2.23">Hag 2:23</reference>). But the Holy Ghost (<reference osisRef="Eph.1.13">Ep 1:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.14">14</reference>). As in <reference osisRef="Song.8.5">So 8:5</reference>, she was "leaning" on Him, that is, her arm on His arm, her head on His bosom; so she prays now that before they part, her impression may be engraven both on His heart and His arm, answering to His love and His power (<reference osisRef="Ps.77.15">Psa 77:15</reference>; see <reference osisRef="Gen.38.18">Ge 38:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.62.3">Is 62:3</reference>).<div eID="gen13164" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13165" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">love is strong as death--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Acts.21.13">Ac 21:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.8.35-Rom.8.39">Ro 8:35-39</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.12.11">Re 12:11</reference>). This their love unto death flows from His (<reference osisRef="John.10.15">Joh 10:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.15.13">15:13</reference>).<div eID="gen13165" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13166" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">jealousy ... the grave--</hi>Zealous love, jealous of all that would come between the soul and Jesus Christ (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.19.10">1Ki 19:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.106.30">Psa 106:30</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.106.31">31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.9.60">Lu 9:60</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.14.26">14:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.16.22">1Co 16:22</reference>).<div eID="gen13166" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13167" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cruel--</hi>rather, "unyielding" hard, as the grave will not let go those whom it once holds (<reference osisRef="John.10.28">Joh 10:28</reference>).<div eID="gen13167" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13168" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">a most vehement flame--</hi>literally, "the fire-flame of Jehovah" (<reference osisRef="Ps.80.16">Psa 80:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.6.6">Is 6:6</reference>). Nowhere else is God's name found in the Song. The zeal that burnt in Jesus Christ (<reference osisRef="Ps.69.9">Psa 69:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.12.49">Lu 12:49</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.12.50">50</reference>) kindled in His followers (<reference osisRef="Acts.2.3">Ac 2:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.15.30">Ro 15:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.2.17">Php 2:17</reference>). <div eID="gen13168" type="x-p"/>

Persecutions (<reference osisRef="Acts.8.1">Ac 8:1</reference>) cannot quench love (<reference osisRef="Heb.10.34">He 10:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.12.15">Re 12:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.12.16">16</reference>). Our many provocations have not quenched His love (<reference osisRef="Rom.8.33-Rom.8.39">Ro 8:33-39</reference>).<div eID="gen13169" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13170" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">if ... give all the substance ... contemned--</hi>Nothing short of Jesus Christ Himself, not even heaven without Him, can satisfy the saint (<reference osisRef="Phil.3.8">Php 3:8</reference>). Nothing but our love in turn can satisfy Him (<reference osisRef="1Cor.13.1-1Cor.13.3">1Co 13:1-3</reference>). <div eID="gen13170" type="x-p"/>

The Gentile Church (<reference osisRef="Ezek.16.48">Eze 16:48</reference>). "We," that is, the Hebrew Church, which heretofore admitted Gentiles to communion, only by becoming Judaic proselytes. Now first idolatrous Gentiles are admitted directly (<reference osisRef="Acts.11.17-Acts.11.26">Ac 11:17-26</reference>). Generally, the saint's anxiety for other souls (<reference osisRef="Mark.5.19">Mr 5:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.4.28">Joh 4:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="John.4.29">29</reference>).<div eID="gen13171" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13172" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">no breasts--</hi>neither faith nor love as yet (see on <reference osisRef="Song.4.5">So 4:5</reference>), which "come by hearing" of Him who first loved us. Not yet fit to be His bride, and mother of a spiritual offspring.<div eID="gen13172" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13173" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">what shall we do--</hi>the chief question in the early Church at the first council (<reference osisRef="Acts.15.23-Acts.15.29">Ac 15:23-29</reference>). How shall "the elder brother" treat the "younger," already received by the Father (<reference osisRef="Luke.15.25-Luke.15.32">Lu 15:25-32</reference>)? Generally (<reference osisRef="2Sam.15.15">2Sa 15:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.9.4">Joh 9:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.9.6">Ac 9:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.6.10">Ga 6:10</reference>).<div eID="gen13173" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13174" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">In the day ... spoken for--</hi>that is, when she shall be sought in marriage (<reference osisRef="Judg.14.7">Jud 14:7</reference>), namely, by Jesus Christ, the heavenly bridegroom. <div eID="gen13174" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8301"/><div sID="gen13175" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8301"/><hi type="bold">9. wall ... door--</hi>the very terms employed as to the Gentile question (<reference osisRef="Acts.14.27">Ac 14:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.2.14">Ep 2:14</reference>). If she be a wall in Zion, founded on Jesus Christ (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.11">1Co 3:11</reference>), we will not "withstand God" (<reference osisRef="Acts.11.17">Ac 11:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.15.8-Acts.15.11">15:8-11</reference>). But if so, we must not "build" (<reference osisRef="Acts.15.14-Acts.15.17">Ac 15:14-17</reference>) on her "wood, hay, stubble" (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.12">1Co 3:12</reference>), that is, Jewish rites, &c., but "a palace of silver," that is, all the highest privileges of church communion (<reference osisRef="Gal.2.11-Gal.2.18">Ga 2:11-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.2.11-Eph.2.22">Ep 2:11-22</reference>). Image from the splendid turrets "built" on the "walls" of Jerusalem, and flanking the "door," or gateway. The Gentile Church is the "door," the type of catholic accessibleness (<reference osisRef="1Cor.16.9">1Co 16:9</reference>); but it must be not a mere thoroughfare but furnished with a wooden framework, so as not merely to admit, but also to safely enclose: cedar is fragrant, beautiful, and enduring. <div eID="gen13175" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8302"/><div sID="gen13176" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8302"/>10. The Gentile Church's joy at its free admission to gospel privileges (<reference osisRef="Acts.15.30">Ac 15:30</reference>, <reference osisRef="Acts.15.31">31</reference>). She is one wall in the spiritual temple of the Holy Ghost, the Hebrew Church is the other; Jesus Christ, the common foundation, joins them (<reference osisRef="Eph.2.11-Eph.2.22">Ep 2:11-22</reference>).<div eID="gen13176" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13177" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">breasts ... towers--</hi>alluding to the silver palace, which the bridal virgins proposed to build on her (<reference osisRef="Song.8.9">So 8:9</reference>). "Breasts" of consolation (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.11">Is 66:11</reference>); faith and love (<reference osisRef="1Thess.5.8">1Th 5:8</reference>); opposed to her previous state, "no breasts" (<reference osisRef="Song.8.8">So 8:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Thess.1.3">2Th 1:3</reference>). Thus <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.46">Eze 16:46</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.16.61">61</reference> was fulfilled, both Samaria and the Gentiles being joined to the Jewish gospel Church.<div eID="gen13177" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13178" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">favour--</hi>rather, "peace." The Gentile Church too is become the Shulamite (<reference osisRef="Song.6.13">So 6:13</reference>), or peace-enjoying bride of Solomon, that is, Jesus Christ, the Prince of Peace (<reference osisRef="Rom.5.1">Ro 5:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.2.14">Ep 2:14</reference>). Reject not those whom God accepts (<reference osisRef="Num.11.28">Nu 11:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.9.49">Lu 9:49</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.15.8">Ac 15:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Acts.15.9">9</reference>). Rather, superadd to such every aid and privilege (<reference osisRef="Song.8.9">So 8:9</reference>). <div eID="gen13178" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8303"/><div sID="gen13179" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8303"/>11. The joint Church speaks of Jesus Christ's vineyard. Transference of it from the Jews, who rendered not the fruits, as is implied by the silence respecting any, to the Gentiles (<reference osisRef="Matt.21.33-Matt.21.43">Mt 21:33-43</reference>).<div eID="gen13179" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13180" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Baal-hamon--</hi>equivalent to the owner of a multitude; so Israel in Solomon's day (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.4.20">1Ki 4:20</reference>); so <reference osisRef="Isa.5.1">Is 5:1</reference>, "a very fruitful hill" abounding in privileges, as in numbers.<div eID="gen13180" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13181" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thousand pieces--</hi>namely, silverlings, or shekels. The vineyard had a thousand vines probably; a vine at a silverling (<reference osisRef="Isa.7.23">Is 7:23</reference>), referring to this passage. <div eID="gen13181" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 11. The joint Church speaks of Jesus Christ's vineyard. Transference of it from the Jews, who rendered not the fruits, as is implied by the silence respecting any, to the Gentiles ( Mt 21:33-43 ). Baal-hamon-- equivalent to the owner of a multitude; so Israel in Solomon's day ( 1Ki 4:20 ); so Is 5:1 , "a very fruitful hill" abounding in privileges, as in numbers. thousand pieces-- namely, silverlings, or shekels. The vineyard had a thousand vines probably; a vine at a silverling ( Is 7:23 ), referring to this passage.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8304"/><div sID="gen13182" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8304"/>12. "mine" by grant of the true Solomon. Not merely "let out to keepers," as in the Jewish dispensation of works, but "mine" by grace. This is "before me," that is, in my power [Maurer]. But though no longer under constraint of "keeping" the law as a mere letter and covenant of works, love to Jesus Christ will constrain her the more freely to render all to Solomon (<reference osisRef="Rom.8.2-Rom.8.4">Ro 8:2-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.6.20">1Co 6:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.5.13">Ga 5:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.2.16">1Pe 2:16</reference>), after having paid what justice and His will require should be paid to others (1Co 7:29-31; 9:14). "Before me" may also mean "I will never lose sight of it" (contrast <reference osisRef="Song.1.6">So 1:6</reference>) [Moody Stuart]. She will not keep it for herself, though so freely given to her, but for His use and glory (<reference osisRef="Luke.19.13">Lu 19:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.6.15">Ro 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.14.7-Rom.14.9">14:7-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.12.7">1Co 12:7</reference>). Or the "two hundred" may mean a double tithe (two-tenths of the whole paid back by Jesus Christ) as the reward of grace for our surrender of all (the thousand) to Him (<reference osisRef="Gal.6.7">Ga 6:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.6.10">He 6:10</reference>); then she and "those that keep" are the same [Adelaide Newton]. But Jesus Christ pays back not merely two tithes, but His all for our all (<reference osisRef="1Cor.3.21-1Cor.3.23">1Co 3:21-23</reference>). <div eID="gen13182" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8305"/><div sID="gen13183" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8305"/>13. Jesus Christ's address to her; now no longer visibly present. Once she "had not kept" her vineyard (<reference osisRef="Song.1.6">So 1:6</reference>); now she "dwells" in it, not as its owner, but its superintendent under Jesus Christ, with vinedressers ("companions"), for example, Paul, &c. (<reference osisRef="Acts.15.25">Ac 15:25</reference>, <reference osisRef="Acts.15.26">26</reference>), under her (<reference osisRef="Song.8.11">So 8:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Song.8.12">12</reference>); these ought to obey her when she obeys Jesus Christ. Her voice in prayer and praise is to be heard continually by Jesus Christ, if her voice before men is to be effective (<reference osisRef="Song.2.14">So 2:14</reference>, end; <reference osisRef="Acts.6.4">Ac 6:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.13.2">13:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Acts.13.3">3</reference>). <div eID="gen13183" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8306"/><div sID="gen13184" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8306"/>14. (See on <reference osisRef="Song.2.17">So 2:17</reference>). As she began with longing for His first coming (<reference osisRef="Song.1.2">So 1:2</reference>), so she ends with praying for His second coming (<reference osisRef="Ps.130.6">Psa 130:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.3.20">Php 3:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Phil.3.21">21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.20">Re 22:20</reference>). Moody Stuart makes the roe upon spices to be the musk deer. As there are four gardens, so four mountains, which form not mere images, as Gilead, Carmel, &c., but part of the structure of the Song: (1) Bether, or division (<reference osisRef="Song.2.17">So 2:17</reference>), God's justice dividing us from God. (2) Those "of leopards" (<reference osisRef="Song.4.8">So 4:8</reference>), sin, the world, and Satan. (3) That "of myrrh and aloes" (<reference osisRef="Song.4.6">So 4:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Song.4.14">14</reference>), the sepulchre of Calvary. (4) Those "of spices," here answering to "the hill of frankincense" (<reference osisRef="Song.4.6">So 4:6</reference>), where His soul was for the three days of His death, and heaven, where He is a High Priest now, offering incense for us on the fragrant mountain of His own finished work (<reference osisRef="Heb.4.14">He 4:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Heb.7.25">7:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.8.3">Re 8:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.8.4">4</reference>); thus He surmounts the other three mountains, God's justice, our sin, death. The mountain of spices is as much greater than our sins, as heaven is higher than earth (<reference osisRef="Ps.103.11">Psa 103:11</reference>). The abrupt, unsatisfied close with the yearning prayer for His visible coming shows that the marriage is future, and that to wait eagerly for it is our true attitude (<reference osisRef="1Cor.1.7">1Co 1:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Thess.1.10">1Th 1:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Titus.2.13">Tit 2:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Pet.3.12">2Pe 3:12</reference>). <chapter eID="Song.8"/><div eID="gen13184" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen12822" osisID="Song" type="book"/>
